discovery: Quantum simulation of strongly correlated many-body systems with ultracold atoms in optical lattices

nominees.name: Immanuel Bloch
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics and Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München, Germany

nominees.name: Peter Zoller
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI, Austrian Academy of Sciences, Austria

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / ultracold quantum gases
motivation: Zoller and co-workers predicted in 1998 that cold bosons in an optical lattice would realize the Bose-Hubbard model and its superfluid-Mott insulator transition. In 2002, Greiner, Bloch and colleagues observed this quantum phase transition. It was the first time a textbook model of strongly correlated matter had been engineered and tuned cleanly in the laboratory. Building on this, Bloch and Greiner developed quantum gas microscopes that image single atoms at single lattice sites. These instruments revealed Mott shells, antiferromagnetic order in the Fermi-Hubbard model, string order, many-body localization and entanglement entropy. Zoller's theory, from cold-atom Hubbard models to synthetic gauge fields, set much of the agenda. Together, their experiments and theory turned analog quantum simulation into a quantitative tool for condensed-matter physics. It is now a worldwide field that tests theory where calculations fail.
